newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. seeks reform to environmental rules.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. seeks reform to environmental rules.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Monday urged the state Legislature to approve reforms to the state's Endangered Species Act to benefit California farmers.
Wilson told the California Farm Bureau Federation's conference in San Diego that reform to the state's Endangered Species Act was long overdue.
"The Legislature can do its part by sending me a bill which ensures that you, the growers and harvesters, are no longer endangered by the Endangered Species Act," Wilson said.
Wilson said agriculture was the cornerstone of the state's economy.
"If we are to succeed in preserving California's heritage and enhancing our economic growth -- we must push ahead with needed reforms and innovations," Wilson, a Republican, said.

Environmental groups have accused the Wilson administration of sponsoring bills to gut the California Endangered Species Act and weaken overall environmental protection by rewriting regulations for species protection.
